messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager -> on-call. SmartRouting anomaly detected for policy 'cost-route-v3'. Unexpected traffic skew to low-cost variant 'mini-q3' on /api/v1/chat/briefing. Eval-failure-rate jumped 0.7% -> 16.4% over 15m. Observed region-fallback flapping between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (multiple rapid switches). Severity: P1. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/smartrouting

riley (oncall): ack. bringing judi and tom in. I see alerts and customer tickets.

tom (eng-runtime): looking at policy diffs: commit 1789000600 enabled cost_delta_smoothing=fast and lowered min_cost_threshold to 0.2. That makes tiny quantized variants much more attractive under transient load.

judi (eng-sre): timeline pls. customer reports?

riley (oncall): change merged 1789000600, first eval alert 1789000685, customer tickets at 1789000720.

priya (customer-success): two customers (FinSage, NovaDocs) reported hallucinated summaries and missing clauses. They've attached examples. They're asking for ETA and whether this was a rollout.

marco (product): any dedicated/reserved tenants affected? need SLA impact assessment.

tom (eng-runtime): checked tags and dedicated pools: none. Hosted api-only. But multiple high-usage accounts hit the affected route.

riley (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable cost-driven fallback for /api/v1/chat/briefing 2) pin route to 'redwood-1.2-large' 3) add a temporary throttle to fallback evaluation to stop region flapping 4) roll back commit 1789000600 in policy repo if necessary. Executing 1 and 2 now.

judi (eng-sre): post commands for audit please.

riley (oncall): running CLI now:

```
redwoodctl policy update cost-route-v3 --set enable_cost_fallback=false --routes /api/v1/chat/briefing
redwoodctl route pin --route /api/v1/chat/briefing --model redwood-1.2-large --reason "emergency pin - quality regression"
redwoodctl routing tweak --set fallback_eval_throttle=30s --policy cost-route-v3
```

rollback-bot: policy-update-apply queued: job 1789001205 on cluster us-east-1. Estimated apply 45s.

riley (oncall): update: policy flag applied, pin job started (job id 1789001212). Throttle set.

rollback-bot: pin-job-1789001212 succeeded at 1789001240. Routing mix reverting.

tom (eng-runtime): I see the model mix shift back to redwood-1.2-large within ~50s. Eval-failure-rate trending down from 16.4% to 5.2% (10m). Region flapping frequency reduced after throttle.

incident-bot: eval-failure-rate: 5.2% (10m) after mitigation; continuing to monitor.

priya (customer-success): informed FinSage and NovaDocs of immediate mitigation and that we are investigating root cause. They asked for a timeline and RCA. I've opened tickets and attached samples.

marco (product): need to understand why commit 1789000600 passed CI. We should require canary quality tests for any change that touches cost normalization.

judi (eng-sre): agreed. ops follow-ups: 1) add alert when model-mix shifts >15% to lower-cost variants within 10m 2) add safety gate to block fast smoothing parameter changes without canary pass 3) document failing-open vs failing-closed behavior for cost fallbacks.

thom (eng-runtime): typo in name; tom (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: cost_delta_smoothing=fast plus lowered min_cost_threshold caused the scoring function to overweight short-term cost drops. Quantized models (mini-q3) have adjustment multipliers that weren't accounted for, so they appeared cheaper than they actually are for quality. Under bursty traffic the weights oscillated, triggering region fallback flapping.

judi (eng-sre): can we repro? write unit/regression tests?

tom (eng-runtime): repro created in canary harness. opened PR to revert smoothing change and add regression tests covering quantized multipliers: https://redwood.internal/policies/PR-2422. Also adding a canary job that runs an expanded promptset for 30m pre-merge.

incident-bot: Customer-impact (preliminary): ~22,400 requests routed to 'mini-q3' across a 20m window. ~7 paying customers reported degraded outputs. Peak user-visible error rate during window ~13%. No evidence of data leakage.

priya (customer-success): offering credits per incident policy and drafting customer comms. Will coordinate approval with legal for wording.

marco (product): owners: RCA & tests - tom, ops/runbook updates - judi, customer comms - priya, product gating - marco. Target: draft postmortem by EOD.

judi (eng-sre): i'm taking watch. riley, can you hand off?

riley (oncall): i need to step out at 10:05. handing off monitoring and follow-ups to judi for 4h. thanks.

judi (eng-sre): taking watch. will run 15m checks and verify pin persists until safe rollout.

rollback-bot: policy-revert PR-2422 merged and staged at 1789001425. Routing changes applied at 1789001450.

tom (eng-runtime): revert applied. started extended canary eval for 45m. tests added.

incident-bot: Post-mitigation status: eval-failure-rate stable at 0.9% (30m). Incident considered mitigated.

priya (customer-success): final customer emails drafted; sending after legal review.

marco (product): follow-ups: add gating + longer canary, adjust default smoothing window, surface quantized adjustment factors in policy schema.

incident-bot: Incident 1789001110 -> RESOLVED (mitigated) at 1789001520. Postmortem template: https://redwood.internal/incidents/templates/pm-template
